newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HOWARD SAYS WIK RULING CLASHES WITH NATIVE TITLE ACT
Prime Minister John Howard says his legal advice is that sections of the Native Title Act are inconsistent with the recent High Court judgement in the Wik case.

John Howard met with state and territory leaders this morning to discuss how the Commonwealth should respond to the ruling, and whether legislation to extinguish native title on pastoral leases should be enacted.
He says in the end all of the groups involved may have to compromise.
200 SEEK HELP AFTER VICTORIAN FIRES
A special recovery centre for victims of the bushfires in the Dandenong ranges, east of Melbourne, is appealing for donations.
More than 200 people affected by the fires have sought help at the recovery centre.
It's giving victims money, clothing, emergency accomodation and counselling.

Spokesperson Lyn Hayes says the idea is to minimise the trauma associated with seeking help from the different agencies. She says financial donations would be appreciated, and people wanting to donate material goods should phone the Shire Council.
PEARSON UNHAPPY ABOUT DISCRIMINATION ACT BEING CHANGED
Aboriginal leader, Noel Pearson, says he hopes the Prime Minister doesn't mean he's prepared to be a racist by suggesting the Racial Discrimination Act may be changed.
Mr Pearson, an advisor to the Cape York Land Council, says anyone who doesn't want to abide by the Racial Discrimination Act is a racist.
Mr Pearson says if it's true the Prime Minister is willing to even contemplate an interference with the Racial Discrimination Act, that's a grave indication of his thinking on this issue.
He was speaking outside a Cairns summit on the High Court's Wik decision.
FISCHER HINTS AT AXING OF RADIO AUSTRALIA
The Deputy Prime Minister says Australia needs to reassess whether there's still a useful role for Radio Australia.
Tim Fischer says the growing dominance of television over radio in developing Asian countries signals a change in times that the ABC's overseas service might not be up to.
Mr Fisher's comments come ahead of the Federal Government's receipt of the Mansfield Report on the A-B-C, which is expected to recommend Radio Australia be dumped.
He says Radio Australia was most successful from the 1950's to 1970's, and he believes it may be time for a change.
ECONOMY SHOWS SLIGHT IMPROVEMENT
The latest measure of where Australia's economy is heading has shown a slight improvement.
The Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index indicates where activity will be in six to nine months time.
The monthly index rose by point-nine points, or point-six percent, in November.
Westpac economists say the key factor was a sharp rise in approvals for non-residential construction, relating to a number of Sydney Olympic projects.
They say apart from this, the trend rise in the index shows the economy will start to grow more strongly by late this year.
KEN ARTHURSON RESIGNS AS ARL CHAIR
Australian Rugby League Chairman, Ken Arthurson has announced his resignation after fourteen years at the helm.
The resignation is effective from February 28.
His departure comes after that of Chief Executive, John Quayle, who's gone to the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games.
Arthurson says the reasons for his departure are that he's reached the age of retirement, he's been advised by a doctor to do so, and he believes it's in the best interest of the game.
BP SAYS IT WON'T USE DEREGULATION TO RAISE PRICES
BP Australia has rejected Federal Opposition claims the company will use petrol deregulation to raise prices.
Managing director, Ronald McGimpsey, says he's extremely concerned the Shadow Competition Minister, Mark Latham, quoted a company letter to resellers out of context.
Mr Latham released details of the letter on Monday, claiming it showed deregulation would give big petrol companies more power, and not lead to lower prices at the pump.
Mr McGimpsey says deregulation will lead to more competition and greater efficiences in the industry, and consumers will benefit.
He says Mr latham's attack is wrong, and particularly offensive to BP.
MUSTER THROUGH TO SEMI FINALS AT OPEN
Austrian Thomas Muster has made it through to the the semi-finals of the Australian Tennis Open, for the second time in his career.
The fifth seed had a convincing win over Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic in three sets, 6-4, 6-2, 6-3, in their quarter finals match.
Muster hasn't reached an Australian Open semi-final since 1989, and will play the winner of tonight's Pete Sampras - Albert Costa match
Meanwhile, in the women's singles, Martina Hingis and Mary Jo Fernandez have also advanced to the semi-finals.
